sections.title: What Is an LIC Maturity Calculator?

content.text: You have an LIC policy and want to know how much it will pay out when it ends. An LIC maturity calculator is an online financial tool that computes the approximate maturity value of your LIC policy by using inputs like your sum assured, policy term, and bonus rates. Think of it as a shortcut – no manual math, no confusion. You simply enter your policy details, and it instantly shows you the projected maturity payout.

For example, industry experts explain that by entering your premium, tenure, and bonuses, the calculator provides an approximate value of the amount you may receive when the policy matures. This helps you plan for life events like education or retirement because you'll know your guaranteed sum plus any declared bonuses. LIC policies are backed by a sovereign guarantee (LIC Act, Sec. 37), meaning the core maturity amount is highly secure. Using our tool, you'll get those numbers in seconds.
How the Calculator Helps You:

items: Quick Estimates: Get instant maturity and bonus values without manual calculations.
Financial Planning: Understand your policy's returns early to compare with other investments.
Policy Check: If you already have a policy, verify its health or see how changes (e.g., paying extra years) affect the payout.
Plan Comparison: Use it across different plans like Endowment or Jeevan Anand.

content.title: Important Note
content.text: This tool calculates the approximate maturity amount including bonuses. It is an estimate. Actual payouts depend on LIC of India's official bonus declarations.

sections.title: How the LIC Maturity Calculator Works

content.text: Under the hood, the maturity calculator applies the standard formula used for traditional LIC endowment policies. It breaks down into three core components:

items: Basic Sum Assured (SA): The guaranteed payout on maturity.
Vested Bonuses: LIC declares a simple reversionary bonus each year (₹ per ₹1,000 SA). Over the policy term, these accumulate.
Final Additional Bonus (FAB): A one-time loyalty bonus paid at maturity for long-term policies.

content.text: Maturity Value = Basic Sum Assured + (Annual Bonus Rate × SA/1000 × Policy Term) + (FAB Rate × SA/1000)
This is the core LIC maturity calculation formula. It assumes that the illustrative bonus rate you enter remains constant each year.

content.text: After using the LIC policy maturity value calculator, you'll see a breakdown of your payout. Here is how to interpret those numbers:

items: Tax-Free Payout: The maturity amount you receive is generally tax-free under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act, provided the annual premium doesn't exceed 10% of the sum assured.
Bonuses: The LIC maturity calculator with bonus includes simple reversionary bonuses added every year. A higher declared bonus rate from LIC means a larger payout.
FAB: The Final Additional Bonus is a loyalty reward. If your policy term is under 15 years, this might be zero. Leave it blank if unsure.

content.text: Note that the payout you actually receive includes these main components (SA + bonuses). If you stop paying premiums early, your policy goes 'paid-up', and the calculator adjusts the results accordingly.

sections.title: Common Scenarios: Surrender, Bonus Changes, Partial Payments

content.text: Surrender: If you exit the policy early, the calculator also shows the guaranteed surrender value and current surrender value. These will be lower than maturity, so you can compare whether to hold or surrender. You can use our dedicated LIC surrender value calculator for an in-depth analysis.
Bonus Changes: LIC bonuses can change annually. If you anticipate higher or lower future bonuses, you can rerun the LIC return calculator with a different bonus rate to simulate scenarios.

Partial Payment (Paid-Up): If you stop paying premiums after at least 2 years, your policy continues as paid-up. The Paid-Up Value is calculated as SA × (premiums paid / premiums payable). You will receive that reduced SA plus bonuses earned up to the stop date.
Loan Eligibility: You can take a loan against your LIC policy. The calculator shows loan eligibility based on current surrender values, helping you secure short-term funds without closing the policy.

sections.title: Pros and Cons of Using an Online Calculator

content.text: Like any financial tool, this calculator has its advantages and limitations:

rows: Fast & Easy: No manual math or waiting for official statements.
Estimates Only: Based on assumed constant bonus rates. Actual bonuses differ.
Planning Aid: Easily compare LIC plans with PPF or mutual funds.
Input Errors: Entering incorrect terms or premiums will skew the results.
Visual Breakdown: See SA, bonuses, and FAB separated clearly.
Not Official: For absolute accuracy, always check LIC's customer portal.

content.text: Overall, the calculator is an excellent educational resource. It gives you a clear understanding of your policy's performance so you can make informed decisions.

The bonus rate is the most important variable in your calculation. LIC declares this rate each year. While not guaranteed, looking at past rates gives a realistic expectation for traditional endowment policies.

Still not convinced? Try a few different scenarios (higher bonuses, longer term) to see how it changes. Then, share your results with an LIC agent or financial advisor. Use our LIC premium calculator to compare new policies, or the retirement corpus calculator for your long-term goals.

items.q: What is an LIC Maturity Calculator?
items.a: An LIC maturity calculator is an online tool that estimates the maturity amount of an LIC policy by using inputs like sum assured, policy term, and bonuses. It saves you from doing manual math.

items.q: How do I calculate the LIC maturity amount?
items.a: The basic formula is: Maturity Value = Basic Sum Assured + (Vested Bonus × Policy Term) + Final Additional Bonus (FAB). You enter your SA, term, and bonus rates into the calculator to compute this value.

items.q: Can I use my LIC policy number in the calculator?
items.a: No. Most online calculators (including ours) require policy details like sum assured, premium, and term. They cannot compute a result from just the policy number.

The calculator provides close estimates based on the data you enter. However, actual maturity amounts depend on official bonus rates and LIC's rules. Use it for planning, but confirm details with LIC.

items.q: Do bonuses count in the maturity value?
items.a: Yes. The maturity value includes the basic sum assured plus all vested simple reversionary bonuses and any Final Additional Bonus (FAB) declared by LIC.

items.q: Is this LIC calculator free to use?
items.a: Absolutely. It's a completely free tool for all BharatSaver users to help you plan better with your LIC policies.

items.q: Does GST affect my maturity payout?
items.a: No. The GST you pay on your premiums does not affect the calculation. The maturity is strictly based on the Sum Assured and declared bonuses.
